mechanisms.name: grain boundary pinning by LPSO phase

evidence.quote: The improved thermal stability in grain boundaries is primarily ascribed to the LPSO phase, which forms during the initial stage of solution treatment and impedes grain boundary migration at temperatures as high as 570 ◦C.

The formation of the LPSO phase at the initial stage of solution treatment obstructs grain boundary migration, thereby imparting thermal stability to the grain boundaries during prolonged heat treatment at elevated temperatures.

Quantitative analysis on strengthening mechanisms reveals that the difference in grain boundary strengthening is the main factor responsible for the strength improvements in Al2Y refined alloys when compared to that of Zr refined counterparts.
The difference in grain boundary strengthening was the key factor that led to the strength improvements in Al2Y refined alloys to that of Zr refined counterparts.
